proxy._note: Caddy for the reverse proxy module. config_file is Caddy's own configuration, written whole from main_template (the distribution's is kept as <file>.pre-freedomnas); tls_dir holds a copy of FreedomNAS's certificate and key readable by group, the group Caddy runs as; sites_dir one file per site from site_template, whose first line (# freedomnas-site owner name port upstream) is what sites_list reads. Templates are str.format strings: literal braces doubled. reload talks to Caddy's admin endpoint (admin in main_template). Names (modules.proxy.names): every site file imports names_dir/*.caddy with its name and upstream; with names on, names_dir holds names_template (one HTTPS site <name>.<domain> on 443 per site, {args[0]} being the imported file's arguments) and sites_dir names.caddy the redirect of http://*.<domain> on 80 and a 404 for names no site has (Caddy matches an exact name before the wildcard); with names off both are removed and the import matches nothing. Names need ports 443 and 80: Arch's caddy.service already grants CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE. Let's Encrypt (modules.proxy.acme): DNS-01 through lego, lego 5 (options after run, which also renews: --renew-days --deploy-hook); acme_secret_write keeps the provider's credentials (env file, sourced) and the deploy hook in acme_dir, root only; acme_obtain gets <domain> and *.<domain> the first time, acme_install copies them where Caddy reads them (acme_tls_dir, its group), acme_cron_template renews daily at 04:<minute> (lego's own random delay kept) with the hook from acme_hook_template; resolvers are public ones, so a Pi-hole answering the domain on the LAN does not confuse the checks.
proxy.sites_list: sh -c 'for f in "$1"/*.caddy; do [ -e "$f" ] && head -n 1 "$f"; done; true' sites_list {dir}
proxy.acme_obtain: sh -c 'set -a && . "$1" && set +a && exec lego run --accept-tos --email "$2" --server "$3" --dns "$4" --dns.resolvers 9.9.9.9:53 --dns.resolvers 1.1.1.1:53 --domains "$5" --domains "*.$5" --key-type EC256 --path "$6" --no-random-sleep' acme_obtain {env_file} {email} {server} {provider} {domain} {path}
proxy.acme_install: sh -c 'install -d -o root -g "$1" -m 750 "$2" && install -o root -g "$1" -m 640 "$3/certificates/$4.crt" "$2/cert.pem" && install -o root -g "$1" -m 640 "$3/certificates/$4.key" "$2/key.pem"' acme_install {group} {tls_dir} {path} {domain}
proxy.acme_hook_template:
#!/bin/sh
# FreedomNAS reverse proxy: put the renewed certificate of {domain} where Caddy reads it, then reload Caddy
set -e
install -o root -g {group} -m 640 {path}/certificates/{domain}.crt {tls_dir}/cert.pem
install -o root -g {group} -m 640 {path}/certificates/{domain}.key {tls_dir}/key.pem
caddy reload --config {config_file} --adapter caddyfile --force
proxy.acme_cron_template:
# FreedomNAS reverse proxy: renew the Let's Encrypt certificate of {domain} (DNS-01) when it has 30 days left
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
{minute} 4 * * * root sh -c 'set -a && . {env_file} && set +a && lego run --accept-tos --email {email} --server {server} --dns {provider} --dns.resolvers 9.9.9.9:53 --dns.resolvers 1.1.1.1:53 --domains {domain} --domains "*.{domain}" --key-type EC256 --path {path} --renew-days 30 --deploy-hook "sh {hook}"' >> {log} 2>&1
